# Adirondack (01, engineer) — SPD-016

## Brief
Objective: three hardenings of the hook path in `bin/spud`, one worktree, each red-first (see `spud ticket show SPD-016` for Desiree's original notes).

1. **Latency.** A hook call costs about 60 ms against the spike's 18 ms, because `bin/spud` (now about 6,400 lines, no suffix) is compiled on every run under `-I -S`, plus its imports. Build a slimmer entry point for `spud hook …` so it lands near 20 ms, without a second copy of any logic: for example the logic moves into an importable module beside the script whose bytecode is cached, and/or heavy imports (argparse, sqlite3, subprocess, fractions, datetime…) become lazy on the hook path. Constraints: it still runs as `python3.14 -I -S <ledger root>/bin/spud hook <Event>` (the script finds SPUD_HOME and any module from its own path, never sys.path or cwd); the suite's "leaves no bytecode" property must still hold for test runs, and any cache must not dirty `git status` (gitignored, or a pycache prefix under `.spud/`, your call, justified in the result). Measure before and after: median of 15 runs each of `PreToolUse(Bash)`, `SessionStart` and `Stop`, same machine, same payloads, and put the table in `member result`. If the hook command line that `settings sync` writes has to change, say so plainly in the result: Spud re-syncs the live settings after merge.
2. **Native deny rules.** `spud settings sync` also writes `permissions.deny` entries `Agent(isolation:*)` and `Agent(model:inherit)`, so Law 3 holds even if the hook is removed or fails to run. Merge exactly like the allow rules: keep foreign entries, no duplicates, idempotent, `--dry-run` prints them and writes nothing. Before coding, confirm the rule syntax against the current Claude Code permissions docs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions or its successor); if the documented syntax differs from these two strings, use the documented form and cite it in the result.
3. **Worktrees elsewhere.** The path rule (around `bin/spud` line 4436) maps only `<home>` and `<home>/.claude/worktrees/<name>/` to repository-relative paths; a worktree made with `git worktree add ../x` counts as outside every project root, where writes are allowed. Map every worktree that `git worktree list --porcelain` names for the ledger root to repository-relative paths, so the deliverable-glob and ledger rules apply there too. Keep the hook budget: measure the git call; cache it if it pushes the hook past the item-1 target, and fail closed where the enforcing hook already fails closed.

Deliverables (only these paths): `bin/**`, `tests/**`, `.gitignore` (only if item 1 needs a cache ignored). Never `.claude/settings.json`, `CLAUDE.md` or anything under `ledger/`, `reports/`, `docs/`.

Read first: `spud ticket show SPD-016`; `CLAUDE.md` sections Ledger v1 (hooks paragraph) and Main and worktrees; in `bin/spud`: `cmd_settings_sync` and the allow-merge helper just above it, the `hook` dispatcher, the path-rule function near line 4436; `tests/test_settings.py`, `tests/test_hooks.py`, `tests/helpers.py`.

Notes: the live hooks run the ledger root's `bin/spud` on `main`, not this worktree's copy, so your edits do not change enforcement while you work. Run the suite from this worktree: `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` (416 tests, about four minutes; run it in the background). Never run `settings sync` without `--dry-run` or against the real `.claude/settings.json`; use `--path` to a temp file.

Done when: each of the three items has a test that failed before its change and passes after; the whole suite is green; the before/after latency table is in `member result`; `settings sync --dry-run --path <temp copy>` output shows both deny rules, pasted in the result.

## Sub-agents

## Ticket proposals
- **Path rule: a case variant of the home path escapes Laws 1 and 5 on macOS** — suggested P1; created as [[SPD-029]] at P1 by Spud.
  Why: map_into_repository compares a Write target with the home (and, since SPD-016, each worktree) by os.path.relpath, which is case-sensitive, and os.path.realpath does not canonicalize case on APFS. On the default case-insensitive filesystem a target spelled with a different-case home prefix, such as /USERS/ERICLUGO/PERSONAL/SPUD/ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md, counts as outside every project root, so the PreToolUse edit hook allows it (and a Bash redirection into it), although it is the same file as the refused ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md. Rooster's HIGH-2 folded case for the part after the root, not for the root itself.
  Evidence: Scratch probe (SPD-016/Adirondack, 2026-09-13), a scratch SPUD_HOME under /private/var/folders, Spud's PreToolUse(Write) to ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md: exact path -> exit 0, deny; the same path with the home prefix upper-cased -> exit 0, silent (allowed). Identical on the pre-SPD-016 bin/spud and on the SPD-016 branch; the filesystem reported samefile(home, home.upper()) true. Fix sketch: when case_insensitive_fs(home), compare roots and targets case-folded (or canonicalize each existing prefix through os.listdir/F_GETPATH), with a test in PreEditTest.

## Result
**Produced** (worktree `spd-016-hook-follow-ups`, uncommitted): `bin/spud`, `bin/spud_ledger.py` (new), `tests/helpers.py`, `tests/test_hooks.py`, `tests/test_settings.py`, `tests/test_launcher.py` (new). `.gitignore` untouched: the caches live under `.spud/`, already ignored.

**1. Latency.** `bin/spud` is now a 47-line launcher; the program moved, unchanged apart from the lines below, to `bin/spud_ledger.py` (no second copy of any logic: the launcher only loads it). The launcher finds the module from its own real path, never sys.path or cwd, and loads it with `SourceFileLoader.get_code` while `sys.pycache_prefix` points at `<home>/.spud/pycache/` (set only around that one call, so stdlib imports keep Python's own caches). `<home>` is SPUD_HOME, else the checkout the launcher sits in; nothing is cached unless `<home>/.spud/` already exists. Why `.spud/` rather than `bin/__pycache__`: it is gitignored, a test run's SPUD_HOME is a scratch directory so the suite leaves no bytecode in the repository, and the hooks refuse edits and shell commands naming `.spud/` exactly as they do for the database, whereas `bin/__pycache__` would be writable by any member with `bin/**`. In the module, `argparse`, `subprocess`, `tempfile`, `hashlib` and `fractions` are imported on first attribute access (a 12-line `LazyModule`; `Fraction(` became `fractions.Fraction(`), and `main` dispatches exactly `hook <Event>` without building the parser. Running `bin/spud_ledger.py` directly exits 2 and names the launcher, so it is no bypass of the Bash hook's `spud` detection.

Worktrees elsewhere.** The path rule maps every worktree that `git -C <home> worktree list --porcelain -z` names, wherever it is, plus the old `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` convention, and the nearest root wins. It checks each root's realpath too, and strips GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE from the git call. A home without `.git` runs nothing. The list is kept in `<home>/.spud/worktrees.json` under a fingerprint that needs no git: the stats of `.git/worktrees` and of each `worktrees/<id>/gitdir`, so add, move, repair and remove all change it. A cold call costs about 16 ms (table), which is why the cache exists. A list git cannot give raises HookError, so the enforcing PreToolUse fails closed (exit 2); recording hooks never call it.
